To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current distribution in noninsulated multi-strand superconductor cables is strongly dependent on the contact resistivity between strands and that the current redistribution and heat diffusion are affected by the current distribution in the quenching process.
The current redistribution in the quench is strongly dependent on the current distribution before the quench and that of the contact resistance between strands.

the current distribution among strands is nonuniform due to the self and mutual inductive coupling between strands, the current redistribution among strands during AC quenching is strongly dependent on the electrical contact resistance at the joint between current lead and the superconducting strand, and the current redistribution among the strands during AC quenches depends on the electrical contact resistivity at the joints between the superconducting strands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of current redistribution and contact resistivity in the quenching process of noninsulated AC superconducting cables with different numbers of strands.
the quench process of AC multi-strand noninsulated superconducting cables and the influence of the contact electrical resistivity at joints on the current distribution and thermal diffusion.
the influence of current distribution on AC quench process in multi-strand superconductor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the AC quench current degrading effect of nonuniform current distribution in noninsulated multi-strand superconductor cable can be reduced by decreasing contact resistivity between superconductor strand and current lead.
the contact electrical resistivity has significant influence on the current redistribution in the quenching process.
the current redistribution among the strands is not significant in the quenching process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

AC loss, contact resistivity, and self and mutual inductor are the main factors that cause the nonuniform current distribution in AC multi-strand cables, and these factors have a strong influence on AC quench current and AC quench time.

the current redistribution in AC noninsulated superconducting cables is strongly dependent on the AC transport current frequency and the contact resistance between strands, and that the current redistribution is more significant in AC noninsulating (6+1) cable.
the current redistribution among the strands and the heat diffusion in the quech process are affected by the contact resistivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current distribution and quench propagation in the noninsulated superconducting cables can be controlled by the contact electrical resistivity between superconducting strand and current lead.

the current distribution among superconducting strands is nonuniform in the AC quench process, and the contact resistivity between superconducting strand and current lead plays a key role in the current redistribution among strands.
the current redistribution and thermal diffusion in the noninsulated AC cables depend strongly on contact resistance between strands.
